reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 FACTORIAL's argument-1 must be an integer in the sense of §1989:A.2.2 AR4 (an arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value: an integer literal, an unscaled numeric elementary item, an integer function, or an always-integral expression; a numeric function is barred by §1989:A.2.3 GR2), so the compiler must accept every such form and refuse a non-integral literal, a scaled item, a numeric function, a non-numeric operand and a not-always-integral expression; the 'greater than or equal to zero' half is a value constraint whose violation makes the reference undefined (§1989:A.2.2 AR4 closing paragraph), so no compile-time refusal is required.

edition-consulted.switches: the IntrinsicSig.IntroducedIn / RemovedIn window; the 1989-module row carries 85, so FACTORIAL binds at --std 85
ArgPredicate.AppliesAt(edition year) for per-position predicates; the FACTORIAL row (Uniform 'i') carries none
EditionInfo.AlphabeticIsAlphanumeric admits class alphabetic in a position whose set holds alphanumeric; the 'i' kind admits numeric only, so the edition-dependent arm is not reached

reader.edition-search: Read IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs (Violation, IntegerViolation, NonIntegralItemReason) and IntrinsicBinder.CheckArgumentClasses / BindFunctionResult; grep Edition|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior|ConstructRegistry|.Year over IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs, IntrinsicBinder.cs, IntrinsicCatalog.cs, IntrinsicCarrierRules.cs, IntrinsicRenderer.cs, FunctionValueLane.cs. IntegerViolation takes ArithmeticMode (an OPTIONS-paragraph setting, native at 85), not the edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the same screen and diagnostics at --std 85 and --std 2023 (intbad.cob run at both); only the expression diagnostic adds '(at COBOL-85 §1989:A.2.2 AR4)'.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f36_01 covers literal, item and integral-expression acceptance and values; the pb5886/pb5891 cases cover not-always-integral expression refusals. Not exercised by the witnesses at 85: scaled item, numeric function, alphanumeric, numeric-edited and group refusals, the P-scaled integer item, and the negative-value (undefined) path; the probes cover them.

reader.notes: The integer screen (IntegerViolation plus the class lattice) refuses every non-integer form at 85 exactly as at 2023, and the runtime computes factorials correctly to 19!. The diagnostic text cites the 2023 clause (§2023:15.36.3 r1) at --std 85 rather than §1989:A.2.14.3 AR1, a wording point only. A negative literal is not refused at compile time, which the 1985 text permits (undefined result).

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 (runs under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-248/runs): rok.cob accepted every integer-typed function argument the 1985 type tables make integer and computed them right: FACTORIAL(FUNCTION MAX(2 3))=6, (MIN(N 4))=6, (SUM(1 2))=6, (RANGE(1 4))=6, (MAX(TE(ALL)))=6, MOD(SUM(TE(ALL)) 4)=1, CHAR(ORD-MAX(3 9 1)+64)=A, FACTORIAL(ZERO)=1, (COMP item)=24, (LENGTH(A))=1, (MOD(7 4))=6, (N**2-6)=6, (+3)=6, (N*2.0)=720. rbad.cob refused (COBOL1627) every numeric-function and non-integer form: MAX(2 3.5), SUM(1 NV), RANGE(1 NV), RANDOM, NUMVAL, REM, MEAN, MIDRANGE, MEDIAN, ANNUITY, SUM(TE(ALL) 0.5), CHAR(PX PIC P9), ALL "1", SPACE, N**0.5, alphabetic item; FACTORIAL(TE(ALL)) refused COBOL1645. redc.cob (class c): 2002 integer functions BYTE-LENGTH, SIGN, INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN and B"1" refused at 85 (COBOL1502/COBOL0900). rsign.cob: SIGN LEADING/TRAILING SEPARATE and COMP operands accepted, MOD(-11 5)=4, MOD(11 -5)=-4, CHAR(PK+62)=A. Cites: OK §1989:A.2.2 AR4 'An arithmetic expression which will always result in an integer value must be specified'; OK §1989:A.2.3 GR2 'A numeric function may not be referenced where an integer operand is required'; OK §1989:A.2.3 GR3 'An integer function can be referenced where an integer operand is required'; OK §1989:A.2.23.1 'The type of this function depends upon the argument types'; OK §1985:VI.6.2.1 'the figurative constant ZERO (ZEROS, ZEROES), such identifiers'.
